Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Solutions Q1 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to StellarTech Solutions’ Q1 2024 earnings call. With me today are Robert Thompson, CEO; Susan Miller, CFO; David Lee, COO; and Alicia Rodriguez, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our press release and earnings slides, which are available on our IR website. Please note that this call may contain forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Robert.

Robert Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet, and welcome, everyone.

We had a strong quarter with performance driven by several key initiatives. First, I’d like to comment on inventory and Days of Inventory, or DOI, for this quarter. As indicated in our preliminary report, Days of Inventory remained stable at 88 days for Q1 2024. While maintaining stability is generally positive, the context surrounding this figure is crucial. We believe this elevated level, sustained now for two consecutive quarters, is a critical area of focus, reflecting a deliberate strategic posture in a volatile global landscape. TSMC anticipates, as previously communicated, that the supply chain will continue to operate with a higher inventory level compared to historical seasonal norms for an extended period. This isn't merely a reflection of inefficiency or overstocking; it's a calculated response to several interconnected factors. While the acute phase of the pandemic has subsided, its ripple effects persist. We continue to see localized lockdowns in key manufacturing hubs in Southeast Asia, particularly Malaysia and Vietnam, impacting the availability of certain critical components. For example, lead times for specific advanced packaging substrates, crucial for our high-performance computing (HPC) chips, have stretched from a pre-pandemic average of 12 weeks to upwards of 22 weeks. This necessitates holding larger safety stocks to mitigate potential production bottlenecks. We project these disruptions will shave approximately 1.5% off potential Q2 revenue if not handled proactively. The ongoing geopolitical tensions, particularly surrounding Taiwan and the South China Sea, create a significant risk to supply chain stability. We are actively diversifying our raw material sourcing and exploring dual-sourcing strategies for critical components. To ensure business continuity, we've increased our strategic buffer inventory of key materials like rare earth elements and specialized chemicals used in advanced lithography by approximately 25% compared to Q4 levels. This increase, while adding to DOI, is a calculated insurance policy against potential disruptions. We are also working closely with governmental bodies to understand and adapt to the changing trade landscape and potential export/import restrictions. Despite macroeconomic headwinds, demand for advanced node technologies remains robust. We experienced a 15% increase in Q1 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, primarily driven by demand from the automotive and high-performance computing sectors. To meet this demand and manage extended lead times for our customers, we are maintaining higher levels of work-in-progress (WIP) inventory. This ensures we can fulfill orders promptly and avoid potential revenue losses due to supply chain constraints. We have observed varying inventory levels across our regional distribution centers. Inventory at our North American distribution centers is currently at 92 days, slightly above the company average, reflecting higher demand from the US market and a proactive strategy to address potential port congestion issues. Conversely, our European distribution centers are operating at a slightly lower DOI of 85 days, due to more efficient logistics and closer proximity to some key suppliers. We are actively working to optimize inventory distribution across our network to minimize storage costs and improve responsiveness to regional demand fluctuations. This includes investment in advanced inventory management software leveraging AI to predict demand more accurately and optimize inventory levels in real-time. We are actively pursuing several technical initiatives to mitigate the impact of elevated DOI on our working capital. We are currently in Phase 2 of the AIMS rollout, which leverages machine learning to predict demand fluctuations and optimize inventory levels across our global network. Preliminary results from Phase 1 indicate a potential reduction in overall inventory holding costs of approximately 5% by Q4 2024. We are strengthening our collaboration with key suppliers through shared data platforms and improved communication channels. This enables us to better forecast demand, plan production schedules, and optimize inventory levels across the entire supply chain. We are also incentivizing suppliers to hold larger buffer stocks on our behalf, reducing our on-hand inventory while ensuring supply security. We are continuously working to reduce cycle times in our manufacturing processes. By streamlining production processes and improving operational efficiency, we can reduce the amount of WIP inventory required to meet customer demand. We are targeting a 10% reduction in overall cycle time by the end of 2025, which will translate into a significant reduction in WIP inventory. While we expect DOI to remain elevated in the near term, we are confident that our strategic initiatives and proactive risk management strategies will mitigate the impact on our financial performance. We are closely monitoring the evolving geopolitical landscape and supply chain dynamics and will adjust our inventory management strategies as needed. We anticipate that by the end of 2025, DOI will decline to 80 days as supply chains stabilize and our efficiency initiatives yield results. We will provide further updates on our progress in future earnings calls. For now, the higher DOI reflects a proactive, considered approach to a complex global environment, designed to ensure continued reliable supply to our customers and sustained revenue growth.

We also made meaningful progress with our Gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Gross margin results v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons. Our gross margin results exceeded expectations, coming in at a robust 55.6%. This represents a significant 2.9 percentage point increase compared to the 52.7% reported in Q4 2023 and a healthy 3.6 percentage point improvement year-over-year from the 52.0% reported in Q1 2023. The substantial QoQ improvement of 2.9 percentage points can be attributed primarily to two key factors. First, StellarTech's ongoing strategy of value selling, particularly in its advanced nodes (N3, N5), continues to bear fruit. We observed a shift in product mix towards higher-margin offerings. For instance, N3 node revenue contributed approximately 24% of wafer revenue in Q1, up from 18% in Q4. This richer mix, coupled with premium pricing for cutting-edge technologies like enhanced N3E variations used in high-performance computing (HPC) and AI applications, added roughly 160 basis points to the gross margin. Specifically, the average selling price (ASP) for wafers incorporating EUV lithography increased by 7% QoQ due to the higher concentration of advanced nodes. Second, our internal cost optimization programs, particularly those focused on energy efficiency and materials usage, yielded tangible results. The "Project Evergreen" initiative, aimed at reducing energy consumption in our fabs, led to a 3% reduction in energy costs per wafer produced. This translates to an estimated 40 basis points positive impact on the gross margin. Furthermore, supply chain efficiencies, including renegotiated contracts with key raw material suppliers (e.g., argon, silicon), contributed another 30 basis points. The 3.6 percentage point improvement YoY stems from a combination of the factors driving the QoQ increase, amplified by the maturity of our advanced node technologies. While advanced nodes are driving ASP increases, we are also seeing margin expansion in more mature nodes (N7, N16) due to increased fab utilization and optimized production processes. For example, N7 utilization rates in our Taiwan fabs climbed to 95% in Q1, compared to 88% in Q1 2023, spreading fixed costs more effectively. The global semiconductor shortage, while easing, still allows StellarTech to maintain a degree of pricing power, especially for mission-critical components used in automotive and industrial applications. This pricing power, although carefully managed to maintain long-term customer relationships, contributed approximately 80 basis points to the YoY gross margin expansion. Three months ago, during our Q4 2023 earnings call, we guided for a Q1 2024 gross margin of approximately 55.1%. Our actual result of 55.6% represents a 50 basis point outperformance. The primary driver of this variance was a more favorable exchange rate than we initially projected. Our guidance was based on an assumed exchange rate of USD 1 to TWD 27.6. The actual average exchange rate for Q1 was USD 1 to TWD 27.95. This difference of TWD 0.35 per USD had a direct positive impact on our reported revenue and profitability when translated back to USD. As noted in the initial summary, this exchange rate difference contributed approximately 50 basis points to the gross margin outperformance. Looking ahead to the second quarter of 2024, we anticipate a further sequential increase in gross margin of approximately 140 basis points, reaching a midpoint of 57%. This positive outlook is driven by the following factors. Our current Q2 guidance incorporates a more favorable exchange rate assumption of USD 1 to TWD 28.8. This stronger TWD is expected to provide a gross margin tailwind of over 100 basis points, as export revenues are boosted when converted back to USD. We expect our cost optimization initiatives and value-selling strategies to continue to contribute positively to gross margins. Specifically, we anticipate further gains from our advanced packaging technologies (e.g., CoWoS, InFO), which are seeing strong demand from AI accelerator manufacturers. We are also rolling out a new AI-powered predictive maintenance system across our fabs, which we estimate will reduce equipment downtime by 5% and further improve cost efficiency. North American customers remain a key driver of our advanced node revenue. Demand for AI-related chips is exceptionally strong, leading to higher average selling prices and favorable product mix. We are closely monitoring geopolitical tensions and working to diversify our customer base to mitigate potential risks. We are seeing increased engagement with European customers, particularly in the automotive sector. Our investment in the European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) in Dresden, Germany, is progressing as planned and will provide a strategic foothold in this important market. While demand from Chinese customers remains significant, we are adhering strictly to export control regulations and ensuring compliance with all applicable laws. We are focusing on serving the domestic Chinese market with mature node technologies. In conclusion, StellarTech's Q1 2024 gross margin performance was strong, driven by a combination of value selling, cost optimization, and a favorable exchange rate. We are confident in our ability to maintain this positive momentum in the coming quarters, supported by our technology leadership, strong customer relationships, and disciplined execution. We will continue to invest in research and development, expand our manufacturing capacity, and optimize our operations to deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

On a broader level, our Operating margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Operating margin results v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons supported our positioning. Today, I'll be providing a comprehensive review of our Q1 2024 operating margin performance, including sequential (QoQ) and year-over-year (YoY) changes, as well as a comparison against our previously issued guidance. We will also discuss the factors driving these results and provide insight into our operating margin guidance for Q2 2024. We are pleased to report a significant improvement in our operating margin for Q1 2024. Our operating margin reached 45.6%, a 3.9 percentage point increase compared to the 41.7% reported in Q4 2023. This positive momentum reflects a combination of factors, primarily related to shifts in our product mix, disciplined cost management, and, notably, a reduction in vaccine donation expenses. The primary driver of the 3.9 percentage point increase sequentially was, as previously mentioned, the substantially lower vaccine donation expense. In Q4 2023, these donations, fulfilling contractual obligations and supporting global health initiatives, represented approximately 7.5% of revenue, translating to $450 million in direct costs. In Q1 2024, this figure decreased to approximately 3.6% of revenue or $220 million. This $230 million reduction directly contributed to the margin expansion. However, it is crucial to note that the improvement wasn't solely due to the vaccine donations. We also saw positive contributions from other areas. Q1 2024 saw a 6% increase in revenue to $6.1 billion, compared to $5.75 billion in Q4 2023. This growth was particularly strong in our Oncology and Cardiovascular therapeutic areas, with a 12% increase in oncology sales driven by the successful launch and adoption of OncoCure and a 9% increase in cardiovascular sales due to continued market penetration of CardioGuard. Our gross margin also saw a slight improvement, increasing by 0.8 percentage points to 78.3%. This was driven by improved manufacturing efficiencies resulting from the Project Phoenix initiative aimed at streamlining our production processes and reducing waste. We are beginning to see the fruits of our investment in automated manufacturing lines at our Dublin facility. We maintained tight control over Selling, General, and Administrative (SG&A) expenses. While SG&A expenses increased nominally by 2% quarter over quarter, this increase was less than the revenue growth rate, leading to a slight decrease in SG&A as a percentage of revenue. We are seeing the benefits of our investment into AI-powered marketing, which is reducing our customer acquisition cost. Looking at the year-over-year performance, our operating margin improved significantly from 42.1% in Q1 2023 to 45.6% in Q1 2024, a 3.5 percentage point increase. This positive change is attributed to the following factors. Consolidated Revenue grew by 11% to $6.1 Billion from $5.5 Billion during the same period last year. In Q1 2023, our Generics division accounted for a larger percentage of overall revenue. This division typically operates at lower margins compared to our Specialty Care and Biologics segments. Our strategic decision to divest certain non-core generics assets at the end of 2023 has naturally shifted our portfolio towards higher-margin products. We strategically divested 3 mature generic products, freeing up capital for faster growth. The acquisition of BioSolutions Inc. in Q2 2023 contributed positively to our operating margin in Q1 2024. The integration of BioSolutions Inc.'s high-margin rare disease portfolio is now complete, and we are realizing the anticipated synergies. We anticipate that these synergies will be worth approximately $100 million by the end of the fiscal year. We continued to drive cost optimization across the organization. Our Lean Manufacturing initiative, implemented in Q3 2023, has yielded significant savings in manufacturing costs, contributing to the margin expansion. During our Q4 2023 earnings call, we guided for an operating margin in the range of 43% to 45% for Q1 2024. We exceeded this guidance, achieving 45.6%. This outperformance was primarily driven by two factors. First, we underestimated the initial market demand for OncoCure, which resulted in higher-than-expected revenue and profitability in the Oncology division. The successful launch was supported by strong clinical data and positive physician feedback. We believe the positive reception will be sustained through the year. Second, we implemented more aggressive cost-cutting measures than initially planned, particularly in areas such as travel and entertainment expenses. This was achieved without compromising our investment in R&D or essential business operations. We leveraged data-driven insights to identify areas of unnecessary spending and implemented more stringent approval processes. Looking ahead to Q2 2024, we anticipate our operating margin to be between 45% and 47%. This guidance reflects our continued focus on revenue growth, cost discipline, and strategic portfolio management. Several factors will influence our Q2 operating margin. We expect continued strong performance in our Specialty Care segment, driven by the continued adoption of OncoCure, CardioGuard and other key products. We plan to increase our R&D investment in Q2 2024 to support the development of our pipeline products. This investment will be targeted at key clinical trials, particularly for our Phase III Alzheimer's drug candidate and our Phase II gene therapy program. We will be closely monitoring the ROI of R&D spending, ensuring we are making the best possible use of our resources. We are closely monitoring currency fluctuations, particularly the strength of the US dollar against the Euro and Japanese Yen. Unfavorable currency movements could negatively impact our operating margin, although we have hedging strategies in place to mitigate some of this risk. We are committed to maintaining tight cost control across the organization. We are continuously looking for opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce expenses. In conclusion, our Q1 2024 operating margin performance was strong, exceeding both our internal expectations and our previously issued guidance. This positive result reflects our focus on revenue growth, cost discipline, and strategic portfolio management. We are confident that we can continue to deliver strong operating margins in the coming quarters. The Q2 guidance reflects our commitment to balancing profitability with strategic investments in R&D and growth initiatives.

I’ll now hand it over to Susan to walk you through the financials.

Susan Miller, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

This quarter’s financial results were underpinned by operational rigor and discipline. Let’s walk through the key metrics.

To start, our CapEx guidance for the full year or long term, the changes from the previous guidance, and the comments for this quarter helped drive improvements in our overall financial health. Today, I want to provide a more in-depth look at StellarTech's capital expenditure guidance, particularly focusing on the unchanged 2024 guidance, the rationale behind it, and the implications for future growth. As you know, StellarTech is maintaining its 2024 capital budget within the range of USD 40 billion to USD 44 billion. This range, initially announced at the beginning of the year, remains unchanged despite the evolving macroeconomic environment and certain short-term fluctuations in demand we've observed in specific sectors. While some might question the consistency of this guidance given the global economic uncertainties, it’s crucial to understand that StellarTech's CapEx strategy is fundamentally driven by a long-term view and anchored in its unwavering commitment to supporting its customers' growth trajectories. The decision to hold firm on the CapEx guidance isn’t arbitrary. It's rooted in several key factors. StellarTech's investments are driven by the fundamental, long-term megatrends shaping the semiconductor industry. These include the proliferation of 5G, the exponential growth of AI and machine learning applications, the increasing electrification of vehicles, and the expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT). These trends are not merely cyclical; they represent fundamental shifts in how technology is being used and, consequently, the sustained demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. StellarTech's capacity expansion plans are meticulously calibrated to the long-term demand profiles of its diverse customer base. We’re not talking about quarterly fluctuations or speculative bets. We’re talking about deeply integrated partnerships with leading technology companies across various sectors. StellarTech engages in extensive, multi-year planning cycles with its key clients, understanding their future product roadmaps and anticipated volume requirements. This collaborative approach ensures that capacity is built where it's needed, when it's needed. StellarTech explicitly avoids building capacity based on short-term market speculation. This is a crucial distinction. Instead of chasing fleeting trends, StellarTech prioritizes sustainable, long-term growth by focusing on the underlying technological drivers and the concrete needs of its customer base. This disciplined approach mitigates the risk of overcapacity and ensures a high utilization rate for its fabs. While we observed some softening in demand for certain consumer electronics applications in Q1, specifically in the lower-end smartphone segment, demand remained robust for high-performance computing (HPC), automotive, and industrial applications. To illustrate, we saw a 15% increase in Q1 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion specifically from HPC applications, driven by the increasing demand for AI training and inference workloads. The automotive sector also grew by 22% year-over-year, reaching $1.8 billion in revenue, fueled by the ongoing transition to electric vehicles and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). The construction of the Arizona fab is progressing on schedule and on budget. The initial phase, focused on 5nm technology, is expected to come online in 2024. The total planned investment in Arizona remains at approximately $12 billion. This investment is critical to serving the growing demand for advanced semiconductors in North America and diversifying StellarTech's manufacturing footprint. The projected revenue from this fab by 2025 is around $3.5 billion, with a potential increase to $6 billion by 2027 as production ramps up and new process technologies are introduced. StellarTech's investment in Japan, in partnership with Sony and Denso, is also proceeding as planned. The fab in Kumamoto will focus on specialty technologies, including 22/28nm processes, catering to the demand for automotive and industrial applications in the region. The rationale behind this investment is to enhance StellarTech's proximity to key customers in Japan and strengthen the overall supply chain resilience. We expect this fab to contribute approximately $1.5 billion in revenue by 2026. Of course, the vast majority of StellarTech's capital investment remains concentrated in Taiwan. The expansion of the Nanke Science Park and the new fabs planned in Kaohsiung are critical to supporting the ongoing ramp of 3nm and the development of even more advanced technologies like 2nm and beyond. These facilities represent the core of StellarTech's technological leadership and will continue to be the primary driver of its long-term growth. The sustained investment in R&D and capacity expansion allows StellarTech to maintain its technological leadership in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. This leadership is crucial for attracting and retaining top-tier customers and commanding premium pricing. We project that StellarTech's gross margin will remain above 50% for the foreseeable future, supported by the high value of its advanced process technologies and its ability to maintain high utilization rates. By proactively investing in capacity based on long-term demand profiles, StellarTech is enabling its customers to innovate and grow. This creates a symbiotic relationship where StellarTech benefits from the success of its customers, and vice versa. While the upfront investment in CapEx is substantial, it ultimately translates into long-term value creation for shareholders. The resulting increase in revenue, profitability, and market share will more than offset the initial investment. In conclusion, StellarTech's unwavering commitment to its capital expenditure guidance, despite short-term market fluctuations, reflects a disciplined and strategic approach to long-term growth. By focusing on fundamental megatrends, collaborating closely with customers, and avoiding speculative capacity, StellarTech is well-positioned to maintain its leadership position in the semiconductor industry and deliver sustained value to its shareholders. We remain confident that the capacity built is designed to support long-term customer growth, ensuring high utilization rates and sustained profitability. We anticipate a strong close to 2024 and a positive outlook for the coming years, driven by the continued demand for advanced semiconductors across a wide range of applications.

Additionally, our Wafer sales and the breakdown to wafer quantity and ASP for this quarter showed strong performance. Q1 2024 saw a 12% increase in overall wafer revenue year-over-year, reaching $2.1 billion. This growth was primarily driven by strong demand for our advanced process nodes, particularly those utilized in high-performance computing (HPC) and mobile applications. While mature nodes remain a stable revenue stream, the significant contribution from 7nm and 5nm technologies highlights our successful transition towards higher-value, leading-edge manufacturing. In Q1 2024, 7nm wafer sales generated approximately $630 million. This represents a slight decrease of 3% compared to Q4 2023, primarily due to increased competition from alternative foundries and a shift in customer demand towards the more advanced 5nm node. However, the 7nm node remains a critical component of our revenue stream, largely driven by applications in AI accelerators, networking infrastructure, and mid-range mobile devices. We shipped approximately 1.2 million 7nm equivalent wafers, resulting in an ASP of around $525 per wafer. Geographically, the demand for 7nm was particularly strong in the Asia-Pacific region, accounting for roughly 65% of 7nm revenue, with significant contributions from Taiwanese and Korean fabless companies. To maintain competitiveness in the 7nm space, we are actively pursuing process enhancements, specifically targeting improved power efficiency and yield optimization. We anticipate a further 5% cost reduction in 7nm production by Q3 2024 through the implementation of advanced metrology techniques and improved defect control. The 5nm node continues to be a significant growth driver, contributing approximately $420 million to our Q1 revenue. This represents a significant 25% increase compared to Q4 2023, demonstrating the increasing adoption of this technology in high-end smartphones, data center GPUs, and other performance-critical applications. We shipped around 600,000 5nm equivalent wafers, yielding an ASP of approximately $700 per wafer. This higher ASP reflects the technological complexity and higher manufacturing costs associated with this node. North America remains the largest market for 5nm wafers, accounting for approximately 40% of the total revenue, driven by major players in the data center and consumer electronics sectors. We are currently focused on expanding our 5nm capacity to meet the escalating demand, investing heavily in new EUV lithography equipment and advanced packaging solutions. We project a further 15% increase in 5nm capacity by the end of Q2 2024. While advanced technologies are the focus of our growth strategy, mature nodes remain crucial for maintaining a stable and diversified revenue base. This segment includes process technologies ranging from 28nm to 180nm, catering to a wide range of applications, including automotive, industrial, and IoT devices. We observed a slight increase of 2% in mature node revenue compared to Q4 2023, driven by strong demand from the automotive sector, particularly for microcontroller units (MCUs) and power management ICs (PMICs). Our 28nm process remains a key contributor within this category, providing a cost-effective solution for a variety of applications. The ASP for mature nodes remains relatively stable, averaging around $150 per wafer. We shipped approximately 4.6 million mature node equivalent wafers this quarter. We are actively exploring opportunities to optimize our mature node manufacturing processes to further reduce costs and improve efficiency. This includes implementing advanced automation technologies and streamlining our supply chain. Our continued investment in EUV lithography is crucial for maintaining our leadership in advanced process technologies. The utilization of EUV in our 5nm and future 3nm processes is enabling us to achieve higher transistor density and improved performance compared to traditional lithography techniques. We are closely monitoring geopolitical developments and their potential impact on our supply chain and customer demand. We are actively diversifying our manufacturing footprint and strengthening our relationships with key suppliers to mitigate potential risks. We are witnessing a growing demand for advanced packaging solutions, such as 2.5D and 3D integration, which are essential for enabling high-performance computing and AI applications. We are investing heavily in these technologies to provide our customers with comprehensive solutions that meet their evolving needs. To address the increasing demand for our advanced process technologies, we are actively expanding our manufacturing capacity in multiple locations. This includes building new fabs and upgrading existing facilities to support the production of 5nm and future process nodes. We anticipate continued growth in our wafer sales throughout 2024, driven by the increasing adoption of our advanced process technologies and the ongoing demand for mature nodes. We remain committed to investing in research and development, expanding our manufacturing capacity, and strengthening our relationships with our customers to maintain our leadership position in the foundry industry. We project a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven by an anticipated ramp-up in 3nm production and continued strength in the 5nm and 7nm segments. We will continue to closely monitor market trends and adjust our strategies accordingly to maximize our profitability and create long-term value for our shareholders.

Now I’ll pass it to David to provide color on execution.

David Lee, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

From a delivery and operations standpoint, this was one of our more efficient quarters in recent memory.

A big part of that was our CapEx, and the CapEx comments for this quarter, which allowed us to increase production capabilities. StellarTech's capital expenditures for the first quarter of 2024 totaled $9.38 billion. This figure represents a 7% decrease compared to the $10.08 billion spent in Q4 2023, but a substantial 22% increase year-over-year compared to the $7.69 billion spent in Q1 2023. The sequential decrease is primarily attributable to the cyclical nature of major equipment installations, which tend to be front-loaded in the second half of the year to meet anticipated demand for the following year. The year-over-year increase underscores StellarTech's continued commitment to expanding capacity and upgrading technology to meet the growing demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Approximately 60% of the Q1 CapEx was dedicated to expanding capacity for leading-edge nodes. This includes the ramp-up of N3 (3nm) production at Fab 18 in Tainan, Taiwan, and initial investments in N3E (enhanced 3nm) capacity in preparation for high-volume manufacturing (HVM) expected to commence in late 2024. Furthermore, a significant portion is earmarked for early-stage tooling and infrastructure for the N2 (2nm) node, with initial pilot production slated for Q4 2024. The N2 node is particularly crucial for StellarTech's long-term competitiveness, promising a 15-20% performance boost and a 30-35% power reduction compared to N3. These investments are primarily focused on securing market share in high-performance computing (HPC), AI, and premium mobile segments. Roughly 25% of the CapEx was allocated to expanding mature node capacity, primarily in response to robust demand from the automotive, industrial, and IoT sectors. StellarTech's investments in 28nm capacity in Nanjing, China, are progressing according to plan, with the facility expected to reach its full production capacity of 40,000 wafers per month by the end of 2024. The expansion addresses critical shortages in power management ICs (PMICs), display driver ICs (DDICs), and microcontrollers (MCUs), particularly those utilized in automotive applications. A smaller portion of this mature node investment is also directed towards expanding 40nm capacity to support analog and mixed-signal applications. Approximately 10% of the CapEx was invested in advanced packaging technologies, specifically CoWoS (Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate) and InFO (Integrated Fan-Out) solutions. This reflects the growing importance of heterogeneous integration in enabling high-performance, low-power systems. Demand for CoWoS packaging, driven by the proliferation of AI accelerators and high-end GPUs, continues to outstrip supply. StellarTech is actively expanding CoWoS capacity at its Zhunan Science Park facility, aiming for a 40% increase in output by the end of 2024. Furthermore, investments in InFO technology are geared towards supporting the growing demand for advanced mobile applications processors. The remaining 5% of the CapEx was allocated to R&D activities and infrastructure improvements, including investments in advanced metrology equipment, environmental sustainability initiatives (e.g., water recycling and energy efficiency projects), and facility upgrades across StellarTech's global manufacturing footprint. StellarTech is facing significant headwinds due to ongoing supply chain disruptions stemming from the continued impact of COVID-19. These disruptions are manifesting in several ways. Tool suppliers are experiencing shortages of critical components, including specialized chips, microcontrollers, and electronic components. This is leading to delays in the delivery of essential equipment to StellarTech. For example, ASML, a key supplier of lithography equipment, has reported delays in the delivery of EUV (Extreme Ultraviolet) lithography systems due to shortages of specific components sourced from multiple vendors. Lockdowns and travel restrictions related to COVID-19 have created labor shortages at various points in the supply chain, impacting manufacturing capacity and extending lead times for critical components. This is particularly acute in Southeast Asia, where many of StellarTech's suppliers have manufacturing facilities. The combined effect of component shortages and labor constraints has resulted in significantly extended lead times for both advanced and mature node equipment. Lead times for some critical equipment have stretched from 12 months to 18 months or even longer. StellarTech is actively working to mitigate these supply chain challenges through a multi-pronged approach. StellarTech is working closely with its tool suppliers to proactively identify potential bottlenecks and develop contingency plans. This includes providing financial support to suppliers to help them expand their capacity and secure critical components. StellarTech is also engaging in joint forecasting and planning exercises to improve visibility and optimize resource allocation. StellarTech is actively working to diversify its supply base and reduce its reliance on single sources for critical components. This includes exploring opportunities to localize component manufacturing within Taiwan and other geographically stable regions. StellarTech has, for example, invested $50 million in a local Taiwanese supplier of specialized valves used in semiconductor manufacturing equipment. StellarTech is strategically stockpiling critical components and materials to buffer against potential supply disruptions. This includes maintaining a buffer stock of key raw materials, such as silicon wafers, chemicals, and gases. StellarTech is exploring the possibility of developing certain critical components in-house to reduce its reliance on external suppliers. This is a longer-term strategy but could provide greater control over the supply chain. StellarTech is maintaining open and transparent communication with its customers regarding potential delays and capacity constraints. This allows customers to adjust their production plans and mitigate the impact of supply chain disruptions. Taiwan remains the primary hub for advanced node manufacturing and R&D. Significant investments are being made in expanding capacity at existing fabs and building new facilities, such as Fab 21 in Kaohsiung. The construction of the Arizona fab is progressing, albeit with some delays due to labor shortages and permitting challenges. StellarTech remains committed to bringing advanced manufacturing capabilities to the US to support domestic demand. StellarTech's joint venture with Sony and Denso in Japan is on track to begin production in 2024. This facility will focus on manufacturing mature node technologies to support the automotive and industrial sectors. The Nanjing fab continues to ramp up production of 28nm chips, addressing the growing demand for mature node technologies in the Chinese market. Despite the near-term supply chain challenges, StellarTech remains confident in its long-term growth outlook. The demand for advanced semiconductors is expected to continue to grow rapidly, driven by the proliferation of AI, 5G, and other emerging technologies. StellarTech's continued investments in R&D and CapEx are essential to maintaining its technology leadership and securing its position as the world's leading semiconductor foundry. Building a more resilient and diversified supply chain is a top priority for StellarTech. The company is committed to working with its suppliers and customers to mitigate the impact of future disruptions.

We also saw execution gains related to our Sales guidance, forecast, or trend by segment next quarter or full year, including improved alignment of production with projected demand. Our analysis of StellarTech's recent commentary indicates a nuanced outlook for revenue growth, characterized by robust performance in specific segments offset by predictable seasonal variations. We project the following for Q2 and the full year. While StellarTech does not provide explicit segment-level guidance, we can infer likely trends based on management's statements. We anticipate HPC to be a significant growth driver in Q2, likely contributing to a 12-15% increase in HPC-related revenue compared to Q1 2024. This growth is fueled by continued demand for advanced processors used in data centers, AI training, and high-end gaming. We project HPC revenues to reach approximately $6.8 billion in Q2, representing roughly 45% of total revenue. Several factors underpin this projection. The insatiable demand for AI processing power drives increased orders for TSMC's leading-edge process nodes (N3, N5) from major AI accelerator vendors like NVIDIA, AMD, and several hyperscale cloud providers. Enterprise data centers are undergoing a server refresh cycle, adopting newer, more efficient CPUs and GPUs which are predominantly manufactured by TSMC. North America and Taiwan-based HPC companies are leading the charge, accounting for the majority of TSMC's HPC revenue. The automotive sector remains robust, experiencing a projected 8-10% sequential growth in Q2. This translates to roughly $1.8 billion in revenue. The automotive industry is continuing to recover from chip shortages. The proliferation of advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), electric vehicles (EVs), and connected car technologies necessitates a higher volume of semiconductors per vehicle. Growing demand from automotive manufacturers in Europe and China further contributes to growth, although China also poses geopolitical risk. TSMC’s specialized automotive-grade processes are in high demand, particularly for safety-critical applications. As anticipated, the smartphone segment will experience seasonal weakness in Q2. We project a 10-12% decline compared to Q1, bringing smartphone revenue down to approximately $3.5 billion. Smartphone OEMs are likely undergoing inventory corrections in anticipation of new model launches in the second half of the year. The global smartphone market is maturing, with slower growth rates in developed regions and increasing competition in emerging markets. Demand in China remains a wildcard, influenced by local brands and economic conditions. IoT segment is expected to maintain a steady growth. We are projecting a 3-5% rise, leading to approximately $1.2 billion in revenue. Continued growth in smart home devices is driving demand for TSMC’s specialty processes, including embedded memory and low-power solutions. The Industrial IoT segment continues to expand, with increasing adoption of connected sensors and devices in manufacturing, logistics, and other industrial applications. aspect_summary.comments on inventory or DOI (Days of In: Days of Inventory (DOI) remained stable at 88 days for Q1 2024. This elevated level is considered strategic due to supply chain volatility, including localized lockdowns and geopolitical tensions. The company increased buffer inventory of key materials by 25% compared to Q4. North American distribution centers have a DOI of 92 days, while European centers have 85 days. The company aims to reduce DOI to 80 days by the end of 2025 through initiatives like AIMS, collaboration with suppliers, and cycle time reduction.
aspect_summary.Gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY c: Gross margin for Q1 2024 was 55.6%, a 2.9 percentage point increase QoQ and a 3.6 percentage point increase YoY. The QoQ improvement was due to value selling in advanced nodes (N3, N5) and cost optimization programs. The YoY improvement was driven by the same factors, amplified by mature advanced node technologies and some pricing power due to the semiconductor shortage. The gross margin exceeded the previous guidance of 55.1% due to a more favorable exchange rate (USD 1 to TWD 27.95 vs. the assumed USD 1 to TWD 27.6). Guidance for Q2 2024 is a further increase to 57%, driven by a more favorable exchange rate assumption (USD 1 to TWD 28.8), cost optimization, and strong demand for advanced packaging technologies.
aspect_summary.Operating margin results, QoQ changes, Y: Operating margin for Q1 2024 was 45.6%, a 3.9 percentage point increase QoQ and a 3.5 percentage point increase YoY. The QoQ increase was primarily due to lower vaccine donation expenses and increased revenue in Oncology and Cardiovascular segments. The YoY increase was attributed to revenue growth, a shift towards higher-margin products through strategic divestments, and the acquisition of BioSolutions Inc. The operating margin exceeded the previous guidance of 43% to 45% due to higher-than-expected revenue from OncoCure and more aggressive cost-cutting measures. Guidance for Q2 2024 is between 45% and 47%, reflecting continued revenue growth, cost discipline, and strategic portfolio management, but also increased R&D investment.
aspect_summary.CapEx guidance for the full year or long: CapEx guidance for 2024 remains unchanged at USD 40 billion to USD 44 billion. This reflects a long-term view driven by megatrends like 5G, AI, electrification of vehicles, and IoT. The company collaborates with customers on multi-year planning cycles. Construction of the Arizona fab is on schedule, and the Japan fab is progressing as planned. The majority of capital investment remains concentrated in Taiwan. This sustained investment aims to maintain technological leadership and command premium pricing.
aspect_summary.wafer sales and the breakdown to wafer q: Wafer revenue increased by 12% YoY, reaching $2.1 billion in Q1 2024. 7nm wafer sales generated $630 million with approximately 1.2 million wafers shipped, resulting in an ASP of $525 per wafer. 5nm node contributed $420 million with around 600,000 wafers shipped and an ASP of $700 per wafer. Mature nodes saw a slight increase and a stable ASP of $150 per wafer with 4.6 million wafers shipped. Continued investment in EUV lithography is crucial for advanced nodes.
aspect_summary.CapEx, and the CapEx comments for this q: Capital expenditures for Q1 2024 totaled $9.38 billion, a 7% decrease QoQ but a 22% increase YoY. 60% was dedicated to expanding capacity for leading-edge nodes, 25% to mature nodes, 10% to advanced packaging technologies (CoWoS, InFO), and 5% to R&D and infrastructure. The company faces supply chain disruptions due to component shortages and labor constraints and is working to mitigate these challenges through diversification, stockpiling, and collaboration with suppliers.
aspect_summary.sales by segment or platforms, their res: While no explicit segment level guidance is provided, commentary suggests HPC is a significant growth driver, Automotive remains robust, Smartphone will experience seasonal weakness, and IoT is expected to maintain steady growth.
aspect_summary.sales guidance, forecast, or trend by se: HPC revenue is projected to increase by 12-15% sequentially in Q2 2024, reaching approximately $6.8 billion. Automotive sector is expected to grow by 8-10% sequentially, translating to roughly $1.8 billion in revenue. The smartphone segment is projected to decline by 10-12% sequentially, bringing revenue down to approximately $3.5 billion. The IoT segment is expected to grow by 3-5%, leading to approximately $1.2 billion in revenue. Overall, Q3 revenue is projected to increase 15% year-over-year to $2.3 billion.
